decisions.title: Feet at last
decisions.situation: You pull off one sock. There was a foot in there the whole time. The other sock now looks suspicious.

result.title: Matching feet
result.body: Two socks off. Ten toes accounted for. You start wiggling them.

journal.text: I pulled off both socks and investigated my toes.

decisions.title: Who said that?
decisions.situation: Your voice echoes in a stairwell. Whoever lives in the walls knows the same words as you, but always says them late.

choices.label: Wait for the walls to start

result.title: A late reply
result.body: The walls return most of your hello. You start again before they finish.

journal.text: I discovered an echo and gave it a very long greeting.

decisions.title: Unlimited dragons, limited shelf space
decisions.situation: At the library, you find a book so big you need both arms to carry it. The return desk suddenly looks very far away.

choices.label: Find a smaller story you love
Ask the librarian for a recommendation

result.title: An ambitious loan
result.body: You finish some of it, skip a confusing chapter, and learn three words you immediately misuse.

journal.text: I borrowed the largest book I could carry.

decisions.title: A very loud rehearsal
decisions.situation: The school alarm sounds during a practice evacuation. Morgan asks everyone to leave calmly. Your chair has other ideas about moving quietly.

choices.label: Follow the instructions and leave your things

result.title: All accounted for
result.body: Morgan checks the class at the meeting point. Your bag can wait inside.

journal.text: I followed Morgan’s instructions during a practice evacuation.

decisions.title: An unclaimed contribution
decisions.situation: A loud fart interrupts the lesson. Alex looks straight at you. Their face suggests a serious conflict of interest.

choices.label: Whisper that the chair needs repairing
Name your prime suspect at full volume

result.title: Lesson continues
result.body: Morgan carries on. Alex eventually stops looking at you.

journal.text: I ignored a suspicious look after a loud noise in class.

decisions.title: The rules have been updated
decisions.situation: You are losing a board game with Morgan. You have just remembered a rule under which you would be winning.

choices.label: Suggest your rule for the next game
Insist it has always been the rule

result.title: A respectable defeat
result.body: Morgan wins this round. You immediately request another.

journal.text: I finished a board game fairly even though I was losing.

decisions.title: The homework needs rinsing
decisions.situation: Your homework went through the wash. Morgan is holding a damp piece of paper that now says almost nothing.

choices.label: Explain and show what you remember
Claim it is an art project

result.title: Second attempt
result.body: You repeat the work and hand it in. This version stays dry.

journal.text: I redid homework that went through the wash.

decisions.title: Glitter lockdown
decisions.situation: You spill a pot of glitter during a class project. Morgan finds some inside a closed book.

choices.label: Make a paper funnel for next time

result.title: Still sparkling
result.body: You clean until the bell. There is probably some glitter left in the building forever.

journal.text: I helped clean a classroom after spilling glitter everywhere.

decisions.title: Imaginary friend wanted
decisions.situation: Alex is alone at break. They say their imaginary friend has moved to a better school. They are interviewing replacements on the empty part of the bench.

choices.label: Pretend you have accidentally sat on one

result.title: A crowded bench
result.body: You reject the first applicant for imaginary biting. Alex rejects the second for actually being a dragon. You run out of break before making an appointment.

journal.text: I helped Alex interview replacements for an imaginary friend.

decisions.title: Little Star, big photograph
decisions.situation: Your school-photo proof arrives. You wore an old top that barely fits. Across your chest, in extremely clear letters, it says “LITTLE STAR”.

choices.label: Ask for a crop above the lettering
Sign the proof like a celebrity
Inspect everyone else’s proof for worse outfits

result.title: Now a very large head
result.body: The cropped proof removes the slogan and most of your shoulders. You approve it before anyone suggests keeping the original as a wallet photo.

journal.text: I cropped an embarrassing slogan out of my school photograph.

decisions.title: Against compulsory naps
decisions.situation: Taylor assigns you to argue against replacing homework with compulsory naps. Alex gets the other side and immediately pretends to fall asleep.

choices.label: Refuse to betray the nap movement

result.title: Evidence against your interests
result.body: You produce a solid argument about lost learning time. A yawn halfway through the speech complicates your position, but the work earns its marks.

journal.text: I prepared a class debate against replacing homework with naps.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Morgan one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Agree on one round each, then stop

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Morgan seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Morgan I would.

decisions.title: The unpaid goblin
decisions.situation: Alex turns your group presentation into a pitch for an imaginary company. You are listed as “unpaid goblin”. Their dog is CEO. Taylor asks where the actual research is.

choices.label: Open the real research before the dog gets a salary
Whisper a demand for a better job title
Delete the pitch while they are presenting it

result.title: Goblin saves the meeting
result.body: You present your actual work. Taylor marks it while Alex clicks past a slide about office beanbags. The dog receives no academic credit.

journal.text: I rescued our group presentation after Alex replaced the research with a fake company pitch.

decisions.title: Do teenagers smell fear?
decisions.situation: Morgan asks you to fix their phone. An open draft says, “Do teenagers smell fear? Mine only appears when the fridge opens.” They suddenly offer to fix it themselves.

choices.label: Offer an answer from a qualified teenager
Fix it without mentioning the draft
Send their contacts a mocking reading of it

result.title: Mostly, we smell cheese
result.body: Morgan laughs and admits they were having a moan. You fix the phone, then both turn towards the sound of the fridge opening.

journal.text: I caught Morgan complaining about me and answered their question about teenagers.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

decisions.title: Did that actually happen?
decisions.situation: During a public reminiscence session, you start telling a vivid story and realise halfway through that part of it might be from a film.

choices.label: Admit you may be mixing memories
Stick to the part you remember clearly

result.title: The audience understands
result.body: Someone else recognises the film. Your actual memory survives with a much smaller car chase.

journal.text: I corrected a memory that had borrowed a scene from a film.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.

journal.text: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Los Angeles offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: a prolonged low mood and loss of interest. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs $540.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: The plan met a different day
decisions.situation: While living with Depression, you reach an optional household task with less energy than you expected. Yesterday’s plan did not allow for that.

choices.label: Choose a smaller version of the task
Leave the optional task and rest
Push through to satisfy the old plan

result.title: A plan that can bend
result.body: You do one manageable part and leave the rest. An incomplete chore feels less important once it stops being a test.

journal.text: I adjusted an optional task to the energy I had with Depression.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Change your position and relax your shoulders

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Los Angeles takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

Keep reopening the chat in horror

result.body: You admit it was rude. The owner replies, “It is on correctly.” Nobody asks which part you meant to apologise for.

journal.text: I apologised after sending a rude wig comment to a group chat.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.
